metaTitle: Sedan, SUV or Van: Which Chauffeur Car to Book in Dubai
metaDescription: Sedan, SUV or van for your Dubai chauffeur? Use seat and luggage counts to choose: sedans take 3 to 4 people, SUVs and vans take 6, all with a fixed fare.
excerpt: Choosing between a sedan, SUV or van in Dubai comes down to two numbers: people and full-size suitcases. This guide matches each Emirates Limo vehicle to the trips it suits, explains how to count luggage properly, and lists the mistakes that leave families stuck at the kerb.
quickAnswer: Choose by capacity, not looks. A sedan suits one to three adults with up to three suitcases, the GMC Yukon SUV takes six passengers and six bags, and a van such as the Mercedes-Benz V-Class gives six seats with a sliding door for pushchairs and older passengers. Count every child as a passenger and every pushchair as a bag, and if you are between two sizes book the bigger car.
content:
Pick the car by counting people and full-size suitcases, not by the badge on the bonnet. In Dubai a sedan covers up to four people with three bags, an SUV takes six people with six bags, and a van gives the same six seats with a sliding door and a walk-in cabin. If you are ever on the line between two sizes, take the bigger one, because a chauffeur car that fits is worth far more than one that looks good in the photo.

Sedan, SUV or van: which chauffeur car is right for you in Dubai?

A sedan is right for one to three adults with a suitcase each, an SUV is right for four to six people or anyone with bulky luggage, and a van is right for families with pushchairs or a group that wants to sit face to face. Emirates Limo lists exact seat and bag counts for every vehicle, and those numbers are the only thing that should decide it. Style is a tiebreaker, capacity is the rule.

What does the Emirates Limo fleet look like at a glance?

GMC YukonSUV66Families, golf and sports luggage, groups who want a high seating position
Kia CarnivalVan55Families with pushchairs, easy access for older passengers
Mercedes-Benz V-ClassVan66Small groups, crews, anyone who wants to work or talk on the move

Every vehicle in the table is chauffeur-driven and reserved for your party alone. The full list with photos is on the Emirates Limo fleet page, and the same six cars are offered whether you book an airport pickup, an intercity run or a chauffeur service in Dubai for the day.

What should I count before I pick a vehicle?

Do this on the sofa before you open the booking form, not in the arrivals hall. Five numbers settle almost every case.

  • Adults and children who need a seat, counting every child as a full passenger
  • Full-size checked suitcases, the ones you cannot lift into an overhead locker
  • Extras that do not stack: pushchairs, golf bags, a bike box, a wheelchair, a cot
  • Child seats needed, by age, so they can be fitted before the chauffeur sets off
  • Whether anyone needs a wide door and a flat floor to get in and out comfortably

Write those five numbers down and hold them against the fleet table above. If people or bags exceed a vehicle's count, that vehicle is out, however much you like it.

When is a sedan the right choice?

A sedan is the right call for one to three adults with one suitcase each and normal hand luggage. The Lexus ES300 takes four passengers and three bags, and the BMW 7-Series and Mercedes-Benz S-Class each take three passengers and three bags. That covers a couple on holiday, an executive with a colleague, or a parent with two teenagers travelling light.

The three-seat count on the BMW and the Mercedes is deliberate. Their rear seats are built for two people to stretch out, and the front passenger seat is the third. If you are booking for a client and want them to have the whole back of the car, a sedan sends the right signal.

Where a sedan falls down is the boot. Three full-size cases fill it, so a fourth bag, a pushchair or a set of golf clubs means a squeeze on the seats or a second car. If your list has any of those extras, skip straight to the SUV.

When do I need an SUV instead of a sedan?

You need an SUV the moment you have four or more people, or four or more full-size bags, or anything bulky. The GMC Yukon takes six passengers and six pieces of luggage, which is double the capacity of a sedan in one vehicle. It is the workhorse of the fleet for families landing at DXB after a long haul.

The Yukon also suits sports luggage and oversized items because the load space is tall as well as long. Two golf bags and four suitcases go in without anyone holding a case on their lap. The high seating position is a bonus on Sheikh Zayed Road, and the rear doors open wide enough for a child seat to be fitted without a struggle.

Book the SUV for a private chauffeur pickup at DXB with your flight number and the chauffeur is inside arrivals with a name board, the flight is tracked, and you get 60 minutes of free waiting time from the actual landing time. Nothing about the vehicle choice changes those terms.

When is a van better than an SUV?

A van beats an SUV when getting in and out matters more than the drive itself. Sliding doors, a low step and a flat floor make the Kia Carnival and the Mercedes-Benz V-Class the easiest cars in the fleet for grandparents, toddlers, anyone with a knee that complains, and pushchairs that need folding at the kerb.

The counts are the same or close: the V-Class takes six passengers and six bags, the Carnival five and five. Where the van pulls ahead is the cabin. You sit upright with room to move, so a family can pass snacks around and a team can open a laptop on the way to Abu Dhabi.

That makes the van the natural pick for an hourly chauffeur in Dubai, where the driver and car stay with you for unlimited stops from AED 150 per hour. Shopping bags go in the back at each mall, children climb in and out without help, and nobody is folding themselves into a rear seat five times in a day.

How do I count luggage properly?

Count checked suitcases, not total items, and picture the biggest bag you own. Emirates sets its checked baggage limit at 32 kg per bag with total dimensions of up to 203 cm, and the airline's checked baggage page spells out the rule. A bag near that limit is what the fleet table means by one piece of luggage.

Cabin bags and rucksacks ride in the footwell or on a lap, so they rarely tip the decision on their own. What does tip it is the awkward stuff: a pushchair counts as a bag, a golf bag counts as a bag of its own, and a bike box or a surfboard needs the SUV or the van no matter how few people are travelling. If you are unsure, message the luggage list on WhatsApp before you book and Emirates Limo will tell you which car fits.

For departures, remember that Dubai Airports recommends being at DXB at least three hours before your flight. Loading six cases into a van at the hotel takes minutes; discovering they do not fit a sedan takes the whole margin.

Does the car I choose change what is included in the price?

No, every vehicle comes with the same all-inclusive fixed fare and the same service. Salik and Darb tolls, VAT and taxes are included in the price you see at booking, and nothing is collected in the car. The UAE government portal notes that Salik applies to every vehicle passing a Dubai toll gate, and that the toll varies by time of day, which is exactly why a fixed fare is worth having.

The fixed price also does not move if the chauffeur sits in traffic or your flight lands late. There is no surge pricing at any hour, and the service runs 24 hours a day including public holidays. Cancel 24 hours or more before pickup for a full refund; inside 24 hours the booking is charged in full.

Waiting time is the same for every car too: 60 minutes free at an airport, 15 minutes free at any other pickup. Child seats are available on request at booking for any vehicle, so ask for one per child when you fill in the form. The Emirates Limo FAQ covers the rest.

What goes wrong when people pick the wrong car?

The most common mistake is counting adults and forgetting that children need seats, so a family of two adults and three children books a three-seat sedan. The second is counting suitcases but forgetting the pushchair, which arrives at the car as a fourth bag with nowhere to go. Both are fixed by the five-number checklist above.

The third mistake is booking the smallest car for a group that will shop. A couple flies in with two cases and leaves for the airport a week later with five, so the sedan that fit on arrival does not fit on departure. Book the two legs separately with different vehicles if your luggage will grow.

The fourth is picking a sedan for a passenger who struggles with low seats. The cars are comfortable once you are in, but a van's sliding door and flat floor make the difference for an older relative or someone recovering from surgery. Dubai Airports has no pick-up area outside arrivals, so the chauffeur walks you to the car park, and a short walk to a van with a low step is far kinder than a stoop into a saloon.

The comparison holds for every route, whether you are heading from the airport to a hotel or booking a private car from Dubai to Abu Dhabi. The drive to Abu Dhabi is around 90 minutes, so on that run the extra legroom of an SUV or van earns its keep even for three people.

faqs.question: How many people fit in a chauffeur sedan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three to four. The Lexus ES300 takes four passengers with three bags, while the BMW 7-Series and Mercedes-Benz S-Class each take three passengers with three bags. Book an SUV or a van for four or more people with luggage.

faqs.question: Which chauffeur car is best for a family with young children in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A van. The Mercedes-Benz V-Class seats six with six bags and the Kia Carnival seats five with five, and both have sliding doors and a flat floor for pushchairs and small children. Child seats are available on request when you book.

faqs.question: Does a chauffeur SUV in Dubai cost more in tolls than a sedan?
faqs.answer: No. Every Emirates Limo fare is fixed at booking and all-inclusive, so Salik and Darb tolls, VAT and taxes are covered whichever vehicle you choose. Nothing is collected in the car, and the price does not change for traffic or flight delays.

faqs.question: How much luggage fits in a GMC Yukon chauffeur SUV?
faqs.answer: Six full-size suitcases alongside six passengers. The tall load space also takes golf bags, a pushchair or a bike box, which is why the Yukon is the usual choice for families arriving at DXB or anyone travelling with sports equipment.

faqs.question: Can I get a child seat in any Emirates Limo vehicle?
faqs.answer: Yes. Child seats are available on request at booking for sedans, SUVs and vans, so add one per child when you fill in the form. Wide-opening rear doors on the SUV and sliding doors on the vans make fitting them straightforward.
